Before it was a physics model it was a studio experiment: frequency-wave patterns locked to a master BPM clock, watched through Blackman–Harris FFT spectroscopy, pulses plotted on a Lorenz attractor with Rayleigh and Prandtl values, metered in RMS, LUFS and TruePeak. The waveforms showed “orbital” state jumps — sudden, consistent pops in the interference pattern that stabilized without collapsing, and stayed invulnerable to collapse as long as frequency changes were held within 100 cents. The question that followed: if an electron's path can't be pinned in space, is it being driven by exactly this kind of interference in time?

VI Cubic time dilation

The Lorentz factor, taken to the cube root

The GNSS proposal replaced the traditional exponent −1/2 with −1/3, originally claimed on the strength of 1,000 simulations against live constellation data — a claim excluded by independent measurement elsewhere in this project (status below). At satellite speeds the models differ by parts in 1011 — exactly the regime where nanoseconds become meters of position error. Push the slider relativistic and watch the two models tear apart.

VII Spin in temporal dimensions

Precession with no field at all

Conventionally, spin precesses because a magnetic field makes it — Larmor precession, defined against spatial axes. Here, spin is a phase object living in the time dimensions, and a mere offset between two clocks, t₁ − t₂, is enough to drive it.

Entanglement is recast the same way — not a spatial correlation stretched across distance, but a temporal correlation: two spinors sharing one phase history across t₁, t₂, t₃.

The clock set: t₁, t₂, t₃ run at independent rates ω₁, ω₂, ω₃, and t₁′ rides at double phase — the octave of t₁ (author-ratified prime convention). Each clock also steps on the zero interval ring in exact π/6 cells, Module XV's θ law brought down to the zero layer: a clock can sit on a coordinate-zero cell or spin through them. Entangling the clocks locks their shared phase history: rates and steps then move the set only in common mode, differences conserved — and since ξ precesses on the clocks' disagreement (ωp = ½ωs(ω₁−ω₂)), entanglement visibly freezes the precession. And what drives root 0? Nothing, by construction: in a layer of zeros an absolute rate is gauge, exactly as an absolute phase is. The animation clock T is a display gauge (ASSUMED), not a master clock; only ratios and differences are physical. The framework-native answer, now author-ratified: root 0 is Module XIII's gearing st : sτ = 2π : 1 — a conversion, not a ticker. The self-referencing zero case is thereby defined: 0·st / 0·sτ inherits the unit ratio because the ratio is scale-free — a removable singularity, not an undefined one. That is partly what two different unit sizes are for: zero cases resolve to the gearing, 2π coordinate radians ≡ 1 proper cycle, instead of dying at 0/0 (FORCED-BY-DEFINITION given the two-unit structure). And the core zeros are not arbitrary neighbours: each sits a major third from the next, so their rates can carry that geometry — Gear M3 locks ω₁ : ω₂ : ω₃ = 1 : 21/3 : 22/3, and the next step of the same chain lands on 2ω₁ — exactly the octave clock t₁′. The prime convention stops being a convention: three thirds close on the octave (FORCED-BY-MECHANICS: (21/3)³ = 2). Each zero carries a ± spin component — the sign of its rate, worn on its label; vertical motion encodes nothing, and pure precession keeps the polar angle fixed.

VIII Temporal hydrogen → two-clock periodic table

Proper time against coordinate time: the atom as a slowed clock

The premise was that an atom could be derived from the relationship between an electron's proper time and the laboratory's coordinate time. It can, exactly. The electron carries its own clock — its Compton phase, ticking at ωC = mc²/ℏ in proper time. A bound state carries a second clock — its energy phase, ticking at E/ℏ in coordinate time. Require them to be the same phase and the energy of every hydrogen-like level is the electron's rest energy slowed by its own time dilation, E = mc² ⟨dτ/dt⟩. The binding energy is the proper time the electron loses; every spectral line is the difference between two clock rates; and the construction holds for one force law only — the inverse square.

Prediction test · zero free parameters · Bohr against proper time —
—

Every atom, not one: the periodic table in proper time

One atom was never enough. The premise extends to the whole table, and at the level of the whole atom it stays exact wherever every interaction is inverse-square: nucleus on electron, electron on electron, as in a Dirac–Slater mean field. The same virial argument that locked hydrogen’s energy to its clock also locks any such atom’s total energy to the sum of its electrons’ proper-time deficits, plus a small term from inside the nucleus (at most 0.6%, at oganesson). Correlation functionals, no-pair many-body Hamiltonians, and QED corrections aren’t inverse-square, so the exact ledger leaves them out. Each electron is then a clock plus a shelter: its clock is set by the charge inside its orbit, and the charge outside exerts no force (Newton’s shell theorem), so it can’t change the clock — it only lifts the energy. Below, all 118 elements are computed that way, with nothing fitted to any of them, and graded against published reference values. So are the clocks that end an atom’s states: radiative decay, which runs on the cube of the transition’s period, and alpha decay, which counts how far the escaping particle falls short of the Coulomb speed.

—
—

Every element is a self-consistent relativistic atom computed offline, nothing fitted: the whole-atom ledger closes to 1.1×10−7 or better for all 118 elements, ionization energy comes in at 5.0% RMS against 99 NIST values, K-shell binding at 0.46% RMS. The largest misses (8–20%, mostly transition metals) trace to local-density exchange's known d/s-electron imbalance, shown rather than trimmed. The same clock-plus-shelter ledger describes, without resolving, the 4s/3d filling-order paradox: calcium's 3d clock runs 3× slower than its 4s but is 94% sheltered, so 4s still lies lower — by scandium the 3d is occupied yet still 0.75 eV above 4s. [OPEN] Radiative decay runs on the cube of the transition period (hydrogen 2p: 1.598 ns, 0.1% from NIST); alpha decay on the Sommerfeld tunneling exponent, fitting 35 even-even emitters to 0.56 decades RMS across 29.8 decades of half-life with one textbook radius and no fitted constant. Two clocks are enough for the whole construction. There's no fitting, and it's exact only for an inverse-square force. Many-electron atoms enter through X-ray screening constants instead, with the Kα doublet as the cleanest proof, since the non-relativistic atom predicts it to be exactly zero. [OPEN] The first edition's fitted t₁ and t₂ sit at round ratios to the Compton clock (1/7.00, 10.01) — rediscovery through rescaling, or three-digit coincidence, left open; t₃ matches no rung. A changing α shifts every atomic line by the same common factor (K = 2), so only the departure K−2 — the proper-time part of Module VIII's atom — can witness it: 3.3×10−5 of Lyman-α in hydrogen, 0.43 in U91+. Optical-clock bounds on α̇/α translate to |S| < 4.4×10−8 on the framework's coupling — seven decades below what "t₃ sets α" would require — so whatever sets α is proper time, consistent with how Module VIII already builds the atom. The fix is to read t³ as the temporal volume t₁t₂t₃ rather than age cubed: letting nc of the three dimensions track cosmic age turns p from a dial into a count, w = nc/2−1, and the observed w = −1.03±0.03 inverts to nc = −0.06 ± 0.06 — a static temporal volume, the only count within reach by seventeen sigma over the next one. X The temporal field equation

General Relativity, given room in time

The centerpiece: an Einstein-type field equation extended with ht² and ht³ perturbation channels, temporal pressure gradients, and quantum-corrected sources. Unfold it in four forms — the fourth, unit-gauged, awaiting ratification.

Well-posedness · ω²(k) of the linearized equation ceff — · damping — · — · Bianchi —
Linearize the same operators the field runs on about its own background amplitude and the mode structure falls out: ω²(k) = ceff²k̂² + m², every coefficient the derivative of a term in the ledger above. Where ω² < 0 the modes grow exponentially instead of propagating — the theory is ill-posed there, whatever the balance meter reads. The instrument reports a real structural constraint rather than a decorative one: the tension pairs' amplitude term (tn/τ)² is anti-restoring, so the framework stays well-posed only while the horizon dressing outweighs it — raise ε, raise α or shorten τ past that point and the long modes go tachyonic. A region of α, ε, R, τ space in which the theory cannot be formulated is a genuine "no", and the sliders above reach it.

The Bianchi check is a second residual, and a stricter one. Because ∇μGμν vanishes identically, any equation of this shape forces ∇μ of everything that is not the Einstein tensor to vanish too — a conservation law the equation imposes on itself. It is not a fit and not a preference: break it and the system has no solutions at all, however neatly the balance meter reads zero. Here ∂x stands in for ∇μ (the reduction's own ASSUMPTION), so the non-Einstein combination must come out spatially constant; the readout above is how far from constant it actually is. It does not read zero, and that is the finding rather than a bug: these terms are assembled one at a time and summed, not varied from a single action, and an action is exactly what would have guaranteed the conservation law for free. Mute terms one by one to see which carry the violation — with everything but curvature muted it falls to exactly zero, which is the check that the meter is measuring what it claims.
Dimensional audit · every term against [Gμν] = L−2 —

The dimensional audit finds two deficit groups closeable from constants the equation already contains: four terms short by L−2 (once the fourth form's gauging is applied) close together under ×1/ℓP², and the source term's shortfall resolves to 1/ℏc — which, since ℓP²/ℏc = G/c⁴, is the same instruction as Einstein's own 8πG/c⁴ coefficient, reached independently. That repair also settles ⟨T⟩'s units: natural units if paired with ℓP², SI stress-energy if paired with 8πG/c⁴, no third option. [OPEN] Less comfortably, the same audit shows h cannot be one field — the channel terms force htn dimensionless while the metric term forces hμν to carry L−2 directly, and both cannot hold for the same object unless they are distinct fields the notation does not currently distinguish. A second, cosmetic ambiguity: the horizon factor's R doubles as the Ricci scalar elsewhere in the same equation; renaming it costs nothing. Full notes in the Manual →

Its significance, in the framework's own terms, lies in combining the geometric curvature of spacetime with dynamic temporal effects — extending the scope of GR to account for:

  • Nonlinear corrections at relativistic and quantum scales.
  • Higher-order time terms — t² and t³ — woven into the spatial-temporal dynamics; the same t³ channel that carries dark energy above.
  • Temporal pressure gradients, dtn/dτ, running from n = −1 upward.
  • Quantum-mechanical source terms: λ₂⟨E²⟩ and λ₃⟨E³⟩ alongside ⟨Tμν⟩, with εₙ/√2 balancing or nullifying channels as regimes demand.
XI Temporal horizons

Where the cubic exponent meets its evidence

This is the module that decides the framework's central kinetic claim, and it is the reason to read it first rather than last. The law is dτ/dt = (1−β²)k with k on trial — GR's ½ against the cubic claim's ⅓. Module VI runs that trial at β² ≈ 1.7×10−10, where the two predictions differ by 3×10−11 and it takes a 145-satellite array and a careful regression to tell them apart. The gravitational form of the same law, dτ/dt = (1−rs/r)k, carries the identical 33% relative split — but onto a quantity physics has been measuring since 1959. In the weak field it gives z = 2k|Φ|/c², so every gravitational-redshift measurement ever made is a measurement of k, and k = ⅓ predicts every one of them coming in a third small. Four anchors below, combined: k̂ = 0.50000 ± 0.00004 — GR at 0.0σ, the cubic exponent at 4762σ, with Gravity Probe A managing it single-handed in 1976. There is exactly one way out and the framework has never said whether it takes it; the panel states it, and cannot choose it for you. The same dressing (1−R/2GM)−1 is the horizon term of the field equation in Module X, and scale symmetry st·sτ = s never breaks: what coordinate time stretches, proper time repays.

Spatialized, the beat lattice is enormous: C4's cross-frame beat wavelength m× = c·|st−sτ| comes to roughly 963 km, halving with each octave up the tonic-return anchors — C5 ≈ 482 km, C6 ≈ 241 km, C7 ≈ 120 km. The double-ruled center band is the tracking lane; the double-bracketed cells are tonic returns.

XIV The temporal volume

Inside the cube: t³ made literal

The three axes of this cube are T₁, T₂, T₃ — not space, but time in three directions. The interior is the cubic-time interference field itself: standing nodes where the three temporal phases agree, voids where they cancel. Drag the cube to turn it, and switch to Cubic mesh to see the geodesic time mesh promoted from its t² surface into full t³ structure — a wireframe that lives in the volume and warps with the field.

volume lit: 38% ·

Interference-node mode is the product field cosω₁T₁·cosω₂T₂·cosω₃T₃ — the same form the Scramble Zone damps with e−γt. Beat-alignment mode sums the phases, and the bright planes are where the temporal beats agree. In Cubic mesh render, the lattice lines are the mesh field itself: every gridline displaces radially with the local field value — the t² surface's undulation, promoted one dimension — so the volume visibly breathes where the phases constructively align. Sweep the T₃ slice and the grid intersections on the plane flare as it passes. Take ω₃ toward zero and the field flattens along T₃: the fine phase relegating itself to the coupling, 1/137. The view-lock planes are the mixed volumetric products: T₁T₂ is the t·τ plane, and the mixed volumes t²·τ and τ²·t are the slabs swept as the T₃ slice travels through them.

XV The harmonic leg

One qubit, strung between τ|0⟩ and t|1⟩

From the canvas panels: a temporal Bloch sphere whose poles are τ|0⟩ (Root; 1) and t|1⟩ at 180°. Ground flip inverts the sphere and the labels with it: τ|1⟩ above, t|0⟩ below. The octave is not a pole at all — it is τ|0⟩′, the τ pole reached again at 360°, and τ|0⟩″ at 720° closes the double cover. The ladder runs 720° at 30° per semitone (π/6 semitone, π/3 wholetone), the yield flipping −i to +i on the second cover. |En⟩m ≠ |En⟩n±m. The superposition plane is not flat: it is a planar volume. Its top face carries one phase, az₁ = φτ, and holds the modal-invariant scale — every interval not in the main set, plus the same root position. Its bottom face carries the second phase, az₂ = φt, and holds the anti-scale — the complement joined with the root and the tritone. Each hemisphere rotates with its own localized gate, or both together under Tgbl for unison motion, as more normal. Drag the sphere to move the state.

The stepwise sequence is interval motion: W H H H H H W W H, wholetones π/3 and semitones π/6 summing to 2π — Tgbl transforms both hemispheres as if unified. The localized T operators rotate each hemisphere independently, forward or backward: anti-transpositionals about the superposition plane. That plane has depth — each azimuth there is a pair. Its top rim is the modal-invariant scaling: always beginning from the same initial state (Root; 1) and processing through each interval not in the main set. Its bottom rim is the anti-scale: the same complement, without respect to the root. Localization without variance permits a maximum unification of two positional types at a time — θ-positional with az₁, or az₁ with az₂; a third coincidence is auto-broken by a semitone. The centripetal cross-section (top right) carries the three point-nodes: state, az₁, az₂. Voice: the amplitudes weight two oscillators — root at the τ pole, √2 at the t pole — and crossing 360° onto cover II lifts both an octave: τ|0⟩′, the root returned primed. The rims read the main set live from Module IV: change the basis there and the modal-invariant and anti-scale faces re-derive here.

XVI The observatory

Every signal, one instrument

The connection layer. Eighteen live quantities from across the engine — the mesh's γ, the Scramble Zone's D(t), the field equation's residual, the attractor's x, the volume's lit fraction, and more — stream onto a single rolling chart. Toggle traces, pick any two, and the correlator computes Pearson's r between them live. Turn on the volume's Lorenz drive and watch the chaos propagate across modules.

Engine telemetry · 60 s window · each trace self-normalized r(A,B) = 0.00
correlate A:
against B:

This is the seed of the synthesis: one clock, many instruments. Signals from modules whose canvases are asleep hold their last value — honest telemetry. Drag the mesh velocity and watch r(γ, Bf) snap toward +1. Correlation only sees what moves: a signal whose section is off screen is a constant, and r against a constant is exactly 0. Where a coupling is real but nonlinear, as when the attractor drives the volume, Pearson can be small even with both moving, and that gap is the kind of thing worth analyzing. Export hands you the raw window as CSV, timestamped, ready for whatever comes next.

Self-audit · the engine against the pages

The ratified canon · laws this build holds

Forced-by-definition
Delineation law
class = semitone mod 4 → C, L₁, M, L₂; tokens are scale degrees — the pages' own equivalences (4 ≡ 5-2i, 7-2i ≡ 6) force the reading. → XIII
Derived · author-ratified
Traveling hat
Ĉ marks the tone at absolute pitch class 0 — the ground-state collapse — never merely a class-C tone; E and G♯ do not wear it. → XIII
Measured · the pages
U-release law
tone k sits over the open cycle (C, E, G♯)ₖ; it releases X → U(Y) iff fret > 0 and its string's open is a chord tone — collapse to the 0ₜ base. → XIII
Forced-by-definition
Zero self-reference
0·sₜ/0·sₛ := sₜ/sₛ = 2π ≡ 1 — the ratio is scale-free, so the singularity is removable; two unit sizes exist partly so 0-cases are defined. → VII
Forced-by-mechanics
M3 gearing ⇒ the prime convention
ω₁:ω₂:ω₃ = 1 : 21/3 : 22/3; three thirds close on the octave, so t₁′ = 2ω₁ is derived, not assumed: (21/3)³ = 2. → VII
Forced-by-mechanics
Lock duality
entanglement conserves differences (phase language); gearing conserves ratios (interval language); both at once over-constrain to a freeze — the additive/multiplicative split of the whole framework, in two buttons. → VII
Forced-by-mechanics
Precession = clock disagreement
ωᵤ = ½ωₛ(ω₁−ω₂); entangling the clocks conserves their differences and visibly freezes ξ; the echo π-kick acts on ξ's azimuth, not the clocks. → VII
Forced-by-mechanics
Spinor double cover
720° = two octaves: 4π periodicity on the harmonic leg; pure precession preserves the polar angle, and each clock wears its spin sign as ± on the label. → XV
Assumed · 1+1D reduction
The field equation runs
the TFE is dynamics, not typography: u̇ = −ρ, ρ = geometric − source; every meter is a measured operator norm from the live field. → X

What the engine has decided · the dynamical claims

These three were live questions when the build started. They are not live now, and the reason each closed is a measurement the framework can check rather than an argument it has to accept.

Excluded · 4762σ
k = ⅓ gravitationally
Every gravitational-redshift measurement is a measurement of k, since z = 2k|Φ|/c². Four anchors combine to k̂ = 0.50000 ± 0.00004; drop the strongest and the other three still give 56.5σ. → XI
Excluded · 854×
the retreat (⅓, ½)
Two exponents make the geoid cancellation fail by (kg−kk)·Δ(v²)/c². TAI has been realised on the geoid since 1972; caesium fountains bound |Δk| < 2×10−4 against the 1/6 required. → XI
Excluded · 51σ
ρΛ ∝ t−3 (nᶜ = 3)
w = p/2−1 gives +½, decelerating. The era objection is closed: matter-era and self-dominated mappings agree iff p(p−3) = 0, so p = 3 is one of the two points where the assumption cannot be blamed. → IX

… and the structural claims, which never depended on them

This is the partition worth carrying forward. Every excluded result above is a claim about dynamics — how fast a clock runs, how a density falls with time. Every result below is a claim about structure — interference algebra, interval arithmetic, a classification rule. The second kind cannot be damaged by the first, because no dynamical parameter appears anywhere in its derivation. A theorem about which ratios make carrier:beat an odd integer is true whatever the exponent on the Lorentz factor turns out to be. So the honest reading of the whole build is not that the framework failed: it is that its dynamical arm is a relabelling of results already measured, and measured well enough to say so, while its structural arm is original work that stands on its own and was never at risk. Invest accordingly.

Theorem · survives untouched
the odd-harmonic law, as an equivalence
carrier:beat = 2b/d + 1 with d = a−b; odd ⇔ d | b, and gcd(a,b)=1 forces d = 1. So the law does not merely hold for superparticular ratios, it characterises them. 5:3 and 8:5 are the two ways it fails, both on screen. → III
Theorem · survives untouched
the delineation law
class = semitone mod 4; 36 of 36 handwritten page headers reproduced live, every build. Pure combinatorics on the pages' own equivalences — no dynamics enter, so no dynamical result can touch it. → XIII
Theorem · survives untouched
M3 gearing and the involution
(21/3)³ = 2 exactly; f(r) = (1+r)/(r−1) is an involution on r > 1, and carrier:beat is invariant under r → 1/r, so that domain is the whole space. Arithmetic, not physics. → VII

Repaired, adopted, or holding

Repaired · constructive
the temporal field equation
Two deficits, each closed by a constant the equation already contains: ×1/ℓP² for four terms, ×1/ℏc for the source. Since ℓP²/ℏc = G/c⁴, the second is the 8πG/c⁴ substitution, found independently. → X
Adopted · three routes agree
nᶜ = 0 — a static temporal volume
Cosmology gives 2(w+1) = −0.06 ± 0.06. A constant α requires it with no cosmology used: clocks cap the coupling at |S| < 4.4×10−8, and only the atom’s proper-time part can witness it. And the framework's own cure for eq (6), A = (t₁t₂t₃)−½, is only a constant if VT is — no observation at all. → IX
Holds · zero free parameters
the temporal atom · E = mc²⟨dτ/dt⟩
Proper clock locked to coordinate clock: exact by the Dirac virial theorem, and for 1/r only. Nothing fitted. H +2.48, He⁺ +8.18, D −3.26 ppm — each the Lamb shift to ≤ 0.08 ppm; Herzberg’s D line closes to +0.05 ppm (±0.25). Moseley RMS 5.7% → 1.05%; the Kα doublet, zero without proper time, to 0.66% for Z ≥ 40. → VIII
Holds · all 118 elements
every atom as a set of clocks
Eatom = Σ mc²(⟨dτ/dt⟩−1) + (inside the nucleus), closed to 1.1×10−7 for every element (Dirac–Slater). Ionization 5.0% RMS over 99 NIST values, K-shell 0.46% over 83, nothing fitted. Decay: τ = 3T³/(32π³αtd²); α half-lives to 0.56 decades over 29.8. → VIII

Open rulings · awaiting the author

θ₀ removal target
cut Module VII's π/6 cell steppers, or Module XV's zero-interval θ entries? Recommendation on file: keep VII, cut XV.
Unit-gauged TFE
adopt sₛ/sₜⁿ on every ladder rung (tier 4, built) — closing the dimensions by the same move that defined 0/0. Ratify or reject.
⟨T⟩ units
ħG/c³ = ℓᵨ² leaves the source term short of L⁻² unless ⟨T⟩ is read in natural units — which is intended?
Scramble Zone's missing static term
the paper's Φ has no static term, so full decoherence sends gravity to zero everywhere unless the cosine product instead modulates a static Newtonian well — the two agree at D=1 and are locally indistinguishable otherwise. Is the missing mean term an omission, or is “gravity decoheres” the intended claim? → V
h is not one field
the dimensional audit forces htⁿ dimensionless while the metric term forces hμν to carry L⁻² directly — both cannot hold for the same object. Are the channel perturbations and the metric perturbation distinct fields the notation doesn't presently say, or is the equation inconsistent before any constant is chosen? → X
t1/t2 ladder coincidence
the first edition's fitted t₁ and t₂ sit at round ratios to the Compton clock, 1/7.00 and 10.01 — rediscovery of the proper clock through a rescaling, or three-digit coincidence? t₃ matches no rung. → VIII
